vo: On chain, a token says one thing. Its issuer says another. Who checks?
Built for teams that hold tokenized Treasuries: asset managers, custodians, compliance.
Every fifteen minutes it reads three funds on Solana: USTB, BUIDL and USDY.
Every row says what was read, from where, and whether it matched. Cannot check is a result too.
Every hour it buys checks through Telegraph, with test USDC on Sepolia: five sanctions screens with receipts, an SEC filing check, and a supply read from Plumb, our own miner.
USTB reconciles exactly on Solana, Ethereum and Plume, and network values land within two dollars of the reported assets. Reckon also lists what it cannot see: the audit, and custody.
BUIDL has no issuer data page, so Reckon says: cannot check.
USDY is flagged: twenty point six percent above the issuer's figure. A gap, not a claim of over-issuance.
After every adjustment, a residual remains. Each explanation is tested in turn. Two Stellar accounts are candidates whose controller is unknown, and nothing is subtracted.
Holdings checks the addresses you hold. These are public examples: balance, value, frozen state, and the findings that follow.
We asked three Claude models five USTB questions, with tools off. Zero of fifteen were exact. They cannot know. Reckon can. One run each, Claude models only.
Reckon reads and compares. It does not audit, and gives no advice. Live now, link on screen.
